Pulses are diverse in their traditional food uses in Asia, Africa, and America, where they are mainly consumed in soups, spreads,
meal components, snacks, and breakfast items (Table 4). As an example, boiled sword beans called “avarakai” in India are consid-
ered an essential food for pregnant women. As well, fried or boiled are the base of the meals of Mesoamerican population, they are
eaten up to three times a day.
Since the common food uses of pulses include them boiled or in soups or stews, one of the most popular industrialized products
is canned cooked beans. For instance, the global market of canned legumes was valued at 2.56 billion of USD in 2019 and it is
expected to grow at 4.0% of annual growth rate (CAGR) from 2020 to 2027. The consumer’s demand for canned legumes has
been increasing as they are a rich source of plant-based proteins (GVR, 2020).
Market trends such as the rise in awareness to increase protein consumption, vegan diets, and the relevance of ethnic food are
stimulating the demand for pulses. The increase of legume consumption is also related to the growth of people looking for alter-
natives to animal protein, besides, the key motivations could be the plant-based food beneﬁts, and awareness of climate change. The
Planetary Health Diet highlights an increased consumption of legumes as one way to move toward sustainable and healthy diets.
